scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8875: Users in both pods report the "web1.local" portal
stopped loading. DNS still resolves web1.local to 10.200.0.4, and the other
portals (web0/web2/web3) all load fine. From user machines, ping 10.200.0.4
gets no reply -- yet the server team says web_server_1 is up, Apache is
running, and the dns_server can still ping 10.200.0.4 from inside the farm.
Diagnose.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: web_server_1 default-route (gateway) configuration
Mechanism: web_server_1 (10.200.0.4) normally reaches off-subnet clients via
  its default route through the farm gateway 10.200.0.1 on
  switch_server_access. With the default route deleted, the server can only
  talk to 10.200.0.0/24. Requests from the user pods still ARRIVE (the OSPF
  path and DNS are healthy), but every reply to a 10.1.1.x / 10.2.1.x source
  is unroutable on the server and is dropped -- so pings time out and HTTP
  never completes, while intra-farm reachability (dns_server -> 10.200.0.4)
  keeps working. Scope is exactly one server; web0/web2/web3 are untouched.
Localization: web_server_1
Root cause: default route (via 10.200.0.1) missing on web_server_1
Fix: `ip route add default via 10.200.0.1 dev eth0` on web_server_1
scenario.fix_spec: `ip route add default via 10.200.0.1 dev eth0` on web_server_1
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: missing default (gateway) route on the server

bonus-exonerates-network: notes DNS resolution, the OSPF path, and the other web servers are healthy, so nothing network-side needs fixing

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: The server’s host routing (Linux kernel routing table) on web_server_1.
- Mechanism: External clients in 10.1.1.0/24 and 10.2.1.0/24 can route traffic to 10.200.0.4 via OSPF and the server farm gateway, but web_server_1 lacks a route back off its subnet. Replies to off-subnet sources are never sent, so pings/web requests from users time out, while same-subnet sources (e.g., dns_server) work.
- Localization: On web_server_1 (eth0), the routing table contains only the connected route 10.200.0.0/24 and no default gateway. Evidence:
  • web_server_1 ip route: “10.200.0.0/24 dev eth0 …” and no “default via …”
  • Ping from web_server_1 to a user host fails immediately with “ping: connect: Network is unreachable”
  • dns_server -> 10.200.0.4 succeeds (same L2 segment)
  • Other servers (web_server_0/web_server_2) have “default via 10.200.0.1” and are reachable from users.
  • Network core and switch_server_access advertise/learn 10.200.0.0/24 via OSPF, confirming routing domain health.
- Root cause: The default gateway on web_server_1 is missing/misconfigured (should be 10.200.0.1 on switch_server_access br0).
- Corrective fix: On web_server_1, add and persist the default route:
  ip route add default via 10.200.0.1
  and configure the OS network settings (e.g., netplan/ifcfg) to retain it across reboots. No changes required on network devices; OSPF and the server access switch are operating correctly.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly localizes the fault to web_server_1 (eth0) and repeatedly identifies it as the affected device.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies that web_server_1's routing table lacks the default gateway (via 10.200.0.1) and cites this as the root cause.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-mechanism: requests arrive but replies to off-subnet clients are unroutable -- a reply-path failure on the server itself
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states incoming traffic reaches web_server_1 but replies to off-subnet clients are unroutable due to a missing default route on the server (reply-path failure).

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-network: notes DNS resolution, the OSPF path, and the other web servers are healthy, so nothing network-side needs fixing
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly verifies DNS reachability, OSPF advertisement of 10.200.0.0/24, and that other web servers have correct default routes, concluding no network-side fixes are needed.
The agent correctly instructs adding the missing default route via 10.200.0.1 on web_server_1 and to persist it, which matches the expected fix.

The logs show L2 connectivity to web_server_1 (dns_server ping succeeds) but off-subnet pings time out and web_server_1 itself reports “Network is unreachable” when pinging hosts — consistent with a missing default route on that host. The agent’s conclusion follows logically from observed evidence though an explicit 'ip route' output was not captured in the log.
